quotes.text: If you expand `balance_transaction` or `latest_charge.balance_transaction`, it might not be available in the response.
Your integration must handle the possibility that the balance transaction might not be immediately available.
use `automatic_async` as the capture method when creating a PaymentIntent.
Our SLA for the charge.updated webhook is 1 hour after the successful PaymentIntent confirmation.

old_evidence.text: set the `capture_method=automatic_async` parameter when confirming a PaymentIntent.

findings: November is a detailed guide and retains the April background-capture model, explicit create-time `automatic_async`, latest-version default wording, initial null fields, events and one-hour `charge.updated` SLA (old lines 8-12, 30-36, 54-76; new lines 9-23, 38-44, 63-86). It adds an explicit operational warning that neither direct nor nested expansion forces deferred data to exist and corrects the event link. No new runtime capture transition is established.

Source line 84 compresses all three fields into a single rule and hides the expanded-field case, webhook destination-charge example and API version boundary. `balance_transaction` applies for asynchronous-capture Charges generally, while `transfer` and `application_fee` are Connect-related. Their appearance in `charge.updated` is specifically annotated for destination charges, rather than a universal Connect charge expectation (new lines 40-61, 84-108; old lines 32-52, 74-97).

Source lines 17 and 22 say PaymentIntent creates an immediate charge without adequate qualification. Source lines 24 and 35 describe manual authorization/capture and asynchronous payment-method states. Preserve them as distinct from `automatic_async`, which can show `PaymentIntent.status=succeeded`, `Charge.captured=true` and a null balance transaction together (new lines 40-76). Response, status and bookkeeping availability do not by themselves establish payout or availability of funds for payout.

Root index line 7 routes via Stripe index lines 23 and 729 to `wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-intents.md`. Its core flow at lines 50-55 and source routes at 134-142 lack a reciprocal async-capture reference.

Adjacent baseline wording is independently compressed: `requires_action` is any further action such as 3DS, not 3DS alone (summary lines 23, 34 and historical lifecycle raw 32-34); source line 86 labels the PaymentIntent client secret server-only despite documented scoped client handoff (raw/stripe-payment-intents-api-2025.md:50-60, 121-125). Keep the merchant API secret server-side and the PaymentIntent client secret customer-scoped.
substantive_changes: New lines 11-17 explicitly cover expanded `balance_transaction` and `latest_charge.balance_transaction` unavailability and make handling missing balance data mandatory. The old guide showed nulls and recommended later events without addressing these explicit expansion requests (old lines 30-52, 68-76). This is added operational guidance, not a newly observed API behavior.

Old raw line 74 displayed `charge.updated` but targeted `charge.created`. New raw line 84 corrects the destination to `charge.updated`, a material navigation correction affecting which event an integrator discovers. The intended event was already evident from old SLA and payload headings (old 68-86); no webhook rename occurred.
historical_claims_to_preserve: April describes faster responses with capture completed in the background and points to explicit `automatic_async` on creation, including create-and-confirm in the example. The standalone opening mentions confirmation (old lines 8-12 and 20-27), but does not by itself establish any confirm-endpoint schema. November centers creation (new 19-36).

The displayed `latest_charge` payment response/webhook shape remains scoped to API version 2022-11-15 or later (old 54-66; new 63-76). That sample cutoff is not the default-capture cutoff. Companion 2024-04-10 changelog gives versioned creation default evidence and includes a 2024-06-20 API reference link (raw/stripe-changelog-2024-04-10-automatic-sync-default-paymentintents-2026-11-07.md:1-22); preserve the guide's 'latest' wording as capture-dated rather than claiming every API or SDK uses this default.

Both captures keep the stated one-hour SLA specifically for `charge.updated` after successful PaymentIntent confirmation, not for payment success, fee/transfer events, settlement or payouts (old 68-76; new 78-86). Preserve additional Connect data handling as applicable to the charge and event.
conflicts: Old event link text and href conflict (old line 74); new line 84 aligns them. Preserve old provenance and warn readers opening the old raw to follow `charge.updated`, not `charge.created`.

The summary's broad immediate-charge shorthand and compressed null-field locator (lines 17, 22 and 84) can mislead state/ledger queries. Add a reciprocal route with the `captured=true`/initial-null coexistence, key Connect qualifiers, and the API-version boundaries. The adjacent April lifecycle paragraph saying funds are now in the account (raw/stripe-payment-setup-intents-2025.md:46-48) is not a promise of populated ledger properties or bank payout.

April Node example explicitly lists `payment_method_types`, while November cURL uses `return_url` and omits that array (old 14-28; new 25-36). This example substitution does not establish a universal `return_url` rule, array prohibition, SDK change, or endpoint removal.
unresolved_questions: No runtime execution, account-specific settlement timing, or support for older unshown webhook shapes is established by the captures.

findings: Give asynchronous capture a discoverable route and preserve both dated captures. Scope creation/default and sample versions separately, retain the expansion constraint and `captured=true`/null coexistence, and list the correct webhook for each applicable deferred field with the stated SLA scope.

Clarify the operation left implicit at source line 84. The April opening says to set `capture_method=automatic_async` when confirming (old raw line 8), while the opt-in text and example put the parameter on PaymentIntent creation with `confirm=true` (old raw lines 10-28). November likewise puts it on creation, including the form-encoded `POST /v1/payment_intents` create-and-confirm example (new raw lines 19-36). These captures do not establish support for the parameter on the standalone confirm endpoint or prove its removal.
conflicts: Source lines 17, 22, 35 and 84 need accurate state and field qualifiers. Cross-link the April `charge.updated` label/`charge.created` href discrepancy to the corrected November target. Independently qualify the old 3DS-only `requires_action` and server-only PaymentIntent client-secret shorthand at lines 23, 34 and 86 using the companion captures.
source_assessments.reason: The materially clarified missing-data behavior and corrected event route merit an update, and the existing merged summary needs an independent correction for field, version and payment-state scope.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 guide at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/asynchronous-capture says `automatic_async` during PaymentIntent creation allows faster confirmation by completing capture in the background. The captured guide calls it the latest API default, so explicit selection is optional there (new raw lines 9-36 and old raw lines 8-28). The pictured succeeded PaymentIntent and captured Charge can precede Charge `balance_transaction` availability even when expanded. The initial attached Charge in the API response and the `charge.succeeded` and `payment_intent.succeeded` events can lack that data. Connect transfer and application fee data may also be deferred, with the later `charge.updated` sample annotating these two fields for destination charges. The example PaymentIntent response and webhook `latest_charge` shape is scoped to version 2022-11-15 or later (new raw lines 38-76 and new raw lines 90-108). Use `charge.updated` for balance transaction and `application_fee.created` and `transfer.created` for applicable Connect objects. The one-hour SLA is for `charge.updated` after successful confirmation (new raw lines 78-86 and old raw lines 68-97). source-stripe-payment-intents.md names the core events but compresses field and version qualifications. Faster response and populated ledger fields are separate, and neither establishes payout.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/asynchronous-capture, November adds explicit nullable expansion-handling instructions and fixes the old `charge.updated` text pointing to `charge.created` (old raw lines 30-52, old raw lines 68-81, new raw lines 11-17 and new raw lines 78-86). This updates integration guidance and navigation without proving a new event or capture transition. The Node-to-cURL example change, example `return_url` and reformatted payloads do not establish new API/SDK requirements (old raw lines 14-28 and new raw lines 25-36). The April opening says to set `capture_method=automatic_async` when confirming (old raw line 8), while the opt-in text and example put the parameter on PaymentIntent creation with `confirm=true` (old raw lines 10-28). November likewise puts it on creation, including the form-encoded `POST /v1/payment_intents` create-and-confirm example (new raw lines 19-36). These captures do not establish support for the parameter on the standalone confirm endpoint or prove its removal. Keep the dated older evidence in source-stripe-payment-intents.md, route to the corrected event, and distinguish latest-API default wording, the separate `2024-04-10` creation-default changelog, and 2022-11-15-or-later sample response coverage (old raw lines 54-66 and new raw lines 63-76). Warn that manual capture and delayed payment-method processing are separate from asynchronous background capture, and that the one-hour availability SLA is stated only for `charge.updated` after successful confirmation (old raw lines 68-76 and new raw lines 78-108). Connect fee/transfer field availability, funds availability, settlement and payout have separate boundaries.
